headline: Tariff refunds are driving corporate strategy and margin protection, while geopolitical tensions in trade deals and port congestion threaten regional supply reliability.

forces.b: Target booked $301 million in tariff refunds this quarter, nearly a fifth of its operating profit, which also boosted earnings despite margin compression elsewhere. Companies risk consumer trust by using these windfalls for employee bonuses rather than inventory investment.

Port congestion in Asia-Europe and Durban is driving medicine shortages, while private sector investment has yet to ease bottlenecks at Durban. A $200 million Maputo port expansion aims to strengthen regional trade gateways amid this infrastructure strain.

India is imposing a 165.2% duty on bulk Scotch imports, while the Quad shrugs off Trump's tariff talk in favor of mineral and sea patrol focus. Carney notes that US trade friction is giving China an edge on EVs, complicating global market access.

Medicine shortages are deepening due to Durban port backlogs, and retailers face stock-out risks during the pre-Lunar New Year peak amid poor reliability. Lowe's earnings show that even tariff refunds could not prevent margin compression.
